failures.question: What is pre-completion OPT?
failures.answer:
Pre-completion OPT is temporary employment authorization for an F-1 student **before completing their academic studies or program**. The employment must be directly related to the student’s major area of study. [1][2]

A student may generally apply after being lawfully enrolled full time for one full academic year at an SEVP-certified school. [2] Pre-completion OPT may be available for up to 12 months, but any time used is deducted from the student’s available post-completion OPT. [1][2]

failures.question: What is an H-1B Labor Condition Application?
failures.answer:
An H-1B Labor Condition Application (LCA) is a Department of Labor filing that an employer submits on Form ETA 9035E or ETA 9035 when seeking to employ a foreign worker in an H-1B specialty occupation or as a fashion model of distinguished merit and ability. [2]

The LCA includes employer-related commitments and supporting information, including documentation used to establish the occupation’s prevailing wage and evidence that required union or employee notifications were made. [2][3] An employer must have filed an LCA for the prospective employment before the H-1B classification applies. [1]

failures.question: What is cap-gap?
failures.answer:
Cap-gap is an automatic extension for certain F-1 students whose timely filed, nonfrivolous, cap-subject H-1B petition requests a change of status and an employment start date in the relevant fiscal year. It extends the student’s F-1 status and eligible employment authorization until April 1 of that fiscal year or the approved H-1B petition’s validity start date, whichever is earlier. [1]

It may apply when the student’s F-1 status and employment authorization would expire before the H-1B change of status takes effect, typically October 1. [2] The extension automatically ends if the H-1B petition or change-of-status request is rejected, denied, revoked, or withdrawn. [1]

results.question: What role does the prevailing wage determination play in PERM?

In PERM, the prevailing wage determination (PWD) establishes the minimum wage that must be offered for the job opportunity so that hiring the foreign worker does not adversely affect similarly employed U.S. workers. [5]

The employer requests the PWD from the National Processing Center (NPC), which determines the appropriate prevailing wage rate. The employer generally must retain the PWD and submit it to the Certifying Officer if requested when filing or processing the PERM application. [4]

If the job is covered by a qualifying collective bargaining agreement, the wage rate in that agreement may be treated as the prevailing wage for labor-certification purposes. [4]
